item.title: Re: The Gods of the SCP Universe
item.content:encoded:
I feel like this ties in to a theme I often enjoy seeing explored within the universe: while the original premise the wiki works seemed to predicate themselves on was that while a unique few might've been aware of such entities, we remained hapless in the face of their might, the idea that in this instance, it's taking that idea of the unknowable dreaming god and flipping it on its head. Oh yes, we do know about them - and not only that, but we've studied them, killed them, turned them into hats, and the genuine battle to take place will be between an enlightened humanity and whatever handlers dreamnt up the Dreamers in the first place.

Thus we ironically (or not-so, considering much of the foundational core that produces content on the wiki) subvert the original impetus for Lovecraft's creative work: sheer, irrational paranoia in the face of strange and alien peoples. We eat their food, we shoot their guns, and we protect them from Fascist, Occultist paramilitary wings. Poetic.

Deep dive into the background of what is theoretically a joke...

So the Centre thinks they worship 001, which is why SPC-140 says this. The truth is more nuanced. They want to literarly eat 001. Which, again, is us.

So just like the Foundation in Swann's proposal, they are trying to transcend narrative layers to get to us. Every time you type "I don't see what the Shark Punching Center has to do with it" when someone mistypes "SPC", I hope you can imagine that a Sharktopusman wants to eat you.

Anyway "Sirpudding's Proposal, I Guess" is on my list of projects that I am trying to get to. I don't know when that will be though.

Does this poem remind you of anything?
Alagadda and Carcosa

Along the shores the cloud waves break,
The twin suns sink beneath the lake,
The shadows lengthen
In Carcosa.
Strange is the night where black stars rise,
And strange moons circle through the skies
But stranger still is
Lost Carcosa.
Songs that the Hyades shall sing,
Where flap the tatters of the King,
Must die unheard in
Dim Carcosa.
Song of my soul, my voice is dead;
Die thou, unsung, as tears unshed
Shall dry and die in
Lost Carcosa.
-Cassilda's Song in The King in Yellow, Act I, Scene 2

item.title: Re: The Gods of the SCP Universe
item.content:encoded:
Not that dumb, if you read the discussion page for Daleport (iirc) there were people who dinged it for directly mixing those canons. So, you know, they might not think so, but it's perfectly valid headcanon.

As far as mythos-type things in the SCP-verse…

+ show block
– hide block

By the very nature of the setting you've got conflicting secret gods/religions that actually impact reality. Scarlet King, Sarkics, Mekhane, Fifthists. A lot of them feel kinda… mundane? I mean, Cthulhu Mythos deities are nearly unaware of humans and operate in a manner that makes human rationality look infantile and pointless. Some early Sarkic stuff was pretty close (e.g., SCP-2480), but since their mythology has been more spelled out, I just kind of see them as people doing fucked up things for essentially rational reasons.

The Fifthists definitely count for me: they and their deity follow a logic that feels completely unmoored from reality.

Also there's things like Alagadda that are as Lovecraft as you can get.

item.title: Re: The Gods of the SCP Universe
item.content:encoded:
The recent Team Bird series features a few different deities and acknowledges them as gods. They are as follows:

  • Thoth: The central deity and antagonist Thoth AKA Sacred Djehuti is a manipulative trickster god, the very same one worshipped by the Egyptians. He imposed his will on the entire human race and conquers worlds to find vassals worthy of his paradise.
  • Medila: As featured in SCP-3095. Medila is an Avian deity that bestows wisdom and intelligence to birds worldwide. Some of the birds affected by this become intelligent enough to be recognized as members of the Foundation, forming the Avian Division.
  • Akheilos: As featured in SPC-507. Known to the Shark Punching Centre as WHITE NETHER, Akheilos is a chaotic Selachian deity that consumes knowledge and is an eternal enemy of Thoth.
  • The Mistaken Beast: (Not actually featured in this series, just alluded to.1) The creator of Akheilos. The Mistaken Beast is a universal Selachian monster that threatens to heavily distort each and every universe, one by one, upon awakening. Sharks are an inherent implausability and humorous plague on reality; the SPC punches them to keep the Mistaken Beast asleep.
Footnotes
1. The Mistaken Beast can be found referenced in the various Shark Punching Center GoI formats on the Wiki.

item.title: Re: The Gods of the SCP Universe
item.content:encoded:
So the Church of the Second Hytoth/Ortothan mythos I've been working has been building up a ton of gods. Only one of them appears as a skip though. For the sake of time this list won't have every detail I've envisioned (more details are in some of the articles), so here are the more prominent gods:

+ Lore galore
- Lore galore

Main Ortothan Mythos Gods

  • The Koru-teusa: The Holy Seven. Seven alien mortals from a now destroyed universe (the 'First Hytoth'), who ascended to godhood and decided to protect the universe from extrauniversal threats (and anything that could threaten themselves or their followers).
    • Zeyu-leusan: The Holy First. Sacrificed themselves to stop a massive extrauniversal incursion.
    • Urkot-leusan: The Holy Second. Killed in a feud with Eov-Leusan.
    • Eov-leusan: The Holy Third. Killed in a feud with Urkot-leusan.
    • Rakmou-leusan: The Holy Fourth. Currently guarding a hole in the universe and fighting extrauniversal threats. The only surviving member of the Koru-teusa.
    • Holy Fifth: Currently unnamed. Status unknown.
    • Yorun-leusan: The Holy Sixth. Former protector of the Eitoth (an afterlife of sorts). Killed during an extrauniversal incursion.
    • Holy Seventh: Currently unnamed. Status unknown; presumed by many to have been wiped out of existence.
  • The Nameless Creator: An extrauniversal "thing" that made the First Hytoth and the Second Hytoth (the current universe). Its intent in creating the universes, whether it is still alive, and whether it is still active is unknown.
  • The One of Dark and the One of Light: Two primordial gods from the First Hytoth, one representing darkness and the other light.1
  • The Voruteut: Not exactly gods but a collection of extrauniversal creatures, deities, and assorted monstrosities that lurk in the space outside the universe (the Voru). This is what the Koru-teusa had been fighting.
  • ???: An unknown extrauniversal "thing" that ate the First Hytoth, destroying it. Status unknown.

Other Gods/Deities

  • Wonlaik the Trickster: A trickster deity that was killed by Rakmou-leusan after their japes went too far.
  • Kornoct: A deity that watches over the Eitoth, essentially serving as its internal security.
  • Uravol the Bodiless: A minor psionic deity in the First Hytoth that went on a massive power trip, killing two of the strongest First Hytoth gods before becoming mentally broken and cast out of any physical form. Status unknown.
  • Nohlos: An ancient First Hytoth god that existed before the universe, eating the reality around itself as it moved through space. Broken into SCP-2742 instances after Uravol attempted to kill it.
  • The God King of the Stars: A powerful god/dictator in the Second Hytoth.2
Footnotes
1. Loosely based on He-Who-Made-Dark and He-He-Made-Light. It doesn't entirely line up with the authorcanon behind those so I now view them as different things.
2. Currently based on Adidal.
